title: Two questions, not one
text: Christians who agree on the creeds still disagree about the "last things". Most of the disagreement comes down to two separate questions. When is the thousand years of Revelation 20? And how should we read the book of Revelation?

title: The inner ring: the millennium
text: Four answers place Christ’s return relative to the "thousand years". He returns after it (postmillennial). The millennium is the present age (amillennial). Or he returns before it (premillennial, in historic and dispensational forms).

title: Postmillennialism
text: Christ reigns now. Through the gospel and the Spirit, the nations will be largely discipled before he returns at the end of a long era of blessing.

title: Amillennialism
text: The thousand years is symbolic of the whole church age. Satan is bound so the gospel goes to the nations, and the saints reign with Christ. One return brings resurrection, judgment and new creation.

title: Premillennialism
text: Christ returns before a future earthly kingdom. Historic premillennialists usually see one return after the tribulation. Dispensationalists distinguish Israel and the church, and most expect a rapture before the tribulation.

title: The outer ring: reading Revelation
text: Preterists see much of the book as fulfilled in the first century. Historicists see it unfolding across church history, futurists mostly at the end, and idealists in timeless patterns. Eclectic readers blend these approaches.

title: The threads: how they combine
text: The axes combine. Gold threads mark common pairings, such as partial preterist with postmillennial, futurist with dispensational, and idealist with amillennial. Dashed threads are rare.
